title: Freeze a round's second-pair candidates, not only their first ordinal
message:
Freeze a round's second-pair candidates, not only their first ordinal

The round plan kept the second pair's first ordinal, but each phase
listed the candidates again from live state. Haste gained after phase 1
inserted the haste candidate and pushed the improved fourth-hand swing
from ordinal 4 to 5, so that swing ran in phase 1 and again in phase 2;
losing haste or a lower weapon could skip candidates instead.

plan_second_pair() now lists the candidates (which hands, haste, bonus
count, trained fourth-hand swings, mirror chance, penalties), and the
round's first routine stores that list in the plan with the first
ordinal. Every phase numbers from the stored list and lets a candidate
swing only while the live list still has it, so a mid-round change adds,
drops or renumbers nothing.

Tests that call phased perform_attacks() directly now start a round per
call, as perform_violence() does.

title: Let unsheath draw what stayed sheathed
message:
Let unsheath draw what stayed sheathed

do_unsheath() refused whenever WIELD_1, WIELD_2H, the offhand or the
shield held anything. After a partial draw (sword drawn, offhand dagger
left sheathed because a held orb took the last hand), freeing the hand
and unsheathing again was refused because of the sword just drawn, and
sheath refused as well, so the dagger was stuck until the sword came off.

The blanket check is gone: unsheath_item() already refuses an occupied
position, a pair conflict or a missing hand for each item, so a later
unsheath draws the remaining item beside the first.

title: Give the third hand's weapon a spare hand after the primary's
message:
Give the third hand's weapon a spare hand after the primary's

is_weapon_wielded_two_handed() doubled a lone third-hand one-hander's
item bonuses whenever any hand was free, and the primary's one-hander
saw the same free hand. Three arms with a +2 STR sword in WIELD_1 and a
+2 DEX sword in WIELD_3 doubled both, while the combat strength bonus
already gave that hand to the primary.

second_pair_spare_hands() now holds the primary-pair-first allocation:
the free hands less the primary's support hand and, with no first-pair
weapon, its unarmed strike. The third hand's item bonuses and its
strength bonus both read it, so that loadout gets +4 STR and +2 DEX at
three arms and both doubled at four.

title: Count unarmed strikes in the third hand's spare hand
message:
Count unarmed strikes in the third hand's spare hand

spare_hand_for_attack() counted only equipped hand positions, so an
unarmed strike took no hand. A three-armed monk with empty hands gave the
primary strike and its support hand and still found a support hand for
the unarmed third strike (+STR+2).

An unarmed primary or third hand now uses one free hand itself: at three
arms the unarmed third hand keeps plain strength, and at four arms it
keeps the bonus only while a hand remains.

title: Draw a round's extra-attack procs once
message:
Draw a round's extra-attack procs once

A round runs perform_attacks() once per phase, and each call rerolled
the extra flurry, Air Embodiment and Wilderness Warrior off-hand procs.
A proc that succeeded in one phase and failed in another moved every
later ordinal, so a second-pair swing could land twice or never.

draw_attack_round_plan() now draws them into char_specials.attack_round
on the round's first attack routine; perform_violence() clears it when
phase 1 begins, and phases 2 and 3 replay it along with phase 1's
second-pair numbering. PHASE_0 routines draw their own.

title: Count arms only for positions that need them
message:
Count arms only for positions that need them

equip_char() checks every position against the arm count and the pair
rule; skip arm_count() for positions that need no arm and for pair
checks with nothing of the other kind in the pair.

title: Retire the implemented arm count plan
message:
Retire the implemented arm count plan

EXTRA_LIMB_MECHANICS.md now records the arm count and its open pricing
work, and the documentation index points there.

title: Document the arm count and rewrite the arm help
message:
Document the arm count and rewrite the arm help

Record the arm count in EXTRA_LIMB_MECHANICS.md, including monk third
hands, provider eligibility and the open Extra Arms pricing. Update the
mechanics, save, race point and Duris documents, both arm feats' text,
and the EXTRA-ARMS and FOUR-ARMS help in help.hlp and the SQL seed.

title: Test the closed-position trim across a deferral
message:
Test the closed-position trim across a deferral

A position closed inside a deferral that ends at the same hand count as
the last completed check must still trigger the hand trim.

title: Replace the four-arm flag with an arm count
message:
Replace the four-arm flag with an arm count

arm_count() now drives every arm-dependent position and the hand budget:
two arms plus a race adjustment, Four Arms (+2), one per Extra Arms rank,
and APPLY_FEAT gear worn in positions the intrinsic arms already open.
wear_slot_arms_needed() replaces is_four_arm_wear_slot(), so counts from
zero up close or open the one-, two-, three- and four-arm positions.

Extra Arms loses its full-BAB melee swing and becomes one arm per rank.
The second weapon pair attacks from three arms up, the fourth hand from
four, and an eligible monk's empty third position strikes unarmed.

The lifecycle becomes limb_reconcile(): closed positions are emptied in
order with the count re-read after each displacement, a third arm splits
a mixed first pair, and a lower hand count trims held items first.
Restoration defers any position the count closes and validates the final
hand budget; save_char() retries postponed positions once.

The wear command picks only open positions, charges a launcher's second
hand, routes two-hand items to the pair's two-hand position and reports
full sets at every count. equip_char() enforces pair exclusivity.
One-hander bonus doubling needs an actual spare hand, and unsheath draws
each item only when a position and the hands are free.

title: Split the casting time scaling out of the racial feat rule
message:
Split the casting time scaling out of the racial feat rule

racial_casting_time() both read the two casting feats and applied the
percentage with its part-tick roll, so the rounding could not serve any
other casting time multiplier. scale_casting_time(casting_time, percent)
now does only the scaling and roll; cast_spell() computes the racial
percentage from the feat ranks at its one call site. No behavior
changes. The part-tick test calls the helper directly without a
character fixture, and the mechanics reference names the helper for
reuse.

title: Scale racial casting speed by 10 percent per rank
message:
Scale racial casting speed by 10 percent per rank

Fast casting and slow casting changed a cast by one whole tick per rank,
so a rank was a 2x change on a one-tick cast and 1.1x on a ten-tick one.
racial_casting_time() now multiplies the casting time by
100 + 10 x (slow ranks - fast ranks) percent, floored at 0: whole ticks
are kept and the fractional remainder is that percent chance of one more
tick, with no roll when the remainder is zero. A race's ranks now match
its Duris spellcast multiplier in both spellcasting time modes. The
adjustment stays ahead of the quicken and other instant-cast overrides.

The feat text, the FAST-CASTING and SLOW-CASTING help entries (help.hlp,
the SQL component, and the dev help database), the mechanics reference,
and the race point prices (0.5 RP per fast rank up to 10, -0.25 RP per
slow rank counted for up to 5) follow the new rule. The tests cover
whole-tick casts through cast_spell() in both modes and the part-tick
roll. The finished plan is removed and the proposal's casting note points
to the mechanics reference.

title: Move the Duris race feat proposal to its own document
message:
Move the Duris race feat proposal to its own document

The proposal for the Duris races not imported leaves the imports record
for docs/ongoing-projects/DURIS_RACE_FEAT_PROPOSAL.md, linked from the
record, the master index, and the player races reference. Its casting
ranks now follow each race's Duris spellcast multiplier at one rank per
10 percent, which the current one-tick-per-rank rule cannot express, so
RACIAL_CASTING_SPEED_PLAN.md plans the change to a percentage rule.
